STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel has a flat centre with a raised rim band and a visible inner wall curving up at the edges, with no deep well. This is a shallow, square bowl (or a square plate with raised edges). I'll treat it as a square shallow dish.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a square dish of this look is typically 20-25 cm across. Judging its overall proportions, it is a medium-to-large serving dish, so I take about 22 cm.
b) Reference cue: the olives are about 2.2 cm long. The olive cluster spans roughly 5 olive lengths across the lower-left area, and the dish's visible width is roughly 10 olive-lengths... the dish spans about 400 px while one olive is about 40-45 px, giving about 9-10 olive lengths, so width ≈ 10 x 2.2 = 22 cm.
Final width: 22 cm (both cues agree).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Kalamata-style olives (dark, pitted-looking): visible count is about 12 whole olives plus 1 small fragment. Pile is about 2 deep in places, so add roughly 3 hidden: about 14 olives. Grams = 14 x 4 g = 56 g.
- Fragment/pit piece: negligible, about 1 g, included in olives.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: The olives sit on the bare floor of the dish with no visible base layer, sauce, or oil, so there is no hidden base layer. Total food is only the olives.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g: Olives (brined, black) ≈ 115-145 kcal/100 g; using 130 kcal/100 g.

Total: 56 g olives.
